• What is orchidectomy/scrotum removal?
  • What is pseudotesticle insertion?
  • Characteristics of orchidectomy, scrotal excision, and pseudotesticular insertion at our hospital
  • Effects of orchidectomy and scrotum removal
  • Effects of pseudotesticle insertion
  • Orchiectomy treatment method
  • Treatment method for pseudotesticular insertion
  • Treatment method for scrotal removal
  • Procedure of surgery
  • Cost of orchidectomy, scrotum removal, and false testicle insertion
  • Precautions after surgery
  • For patients visiting from far away

What is orchidectomy/scrotum removal?

Literally, removing the testicles is called "orchidectomy." With the loss of testicles, the male hormone testosterone decreases, leading to a progressive feminization of the mind and body.
At our hospital, we perform orchidectomy for people who suffer from gender identity disorder and are averse to having male genitalia, or who want to fully experience the effects of administering female hormones.
Note that if you just remove the testicles, the scrotum will stretch and become more noticeable when it warms up. In order to achieve a clearer look, we recommend that you also undergo scrotal removal surgery, which involves removing the scrotum.

If this is the case, please contact our hospital.

Orchiectomy and scrotum removal are often requested in the following cases:
If you have any other concerns or goals, please feel free to contact our clinic.

  • have gender identity disorder
  • It's not that I want to be a woman, but I feel uncomfortable being a man.
  • I want to be androgynous
  • I want to lower testosterone and prevent thinning hair.
  • I want to keep my groin area clean.
A diagnosis of gender identity disorder is required for surgery.
Risks and side effects of orchiectomy

Bleeding, infection, pain, and swelling may occur, and if both testicles are removed, the drop in male hormones may cause problems such as decreased libido, decreased erectile function, hot flashes, sweating, and infertility.

Risks and side effects of scrotal removal

Bleeding, hematoma, infection, scars, left-right disparity, sensory changes, feeling of tightness, impact on surrounding tissues

What is pseudotesticle insertion?

To solve the cosmetic problem of people who have lost one testicle due to some reason, a silicone pseudotesticle is inserted into the scrotum.

If this is the case, please contact our hospital.

  • Testicles removed due to trauma
  • Testicles removed due to testicular cancer, acute scrofula, etc.
  • Born without testicles

 

Characteristics of orchidectomy, scrotal excision, and pseudotesticular insertion at our hospital

1. Completely private room

Examinations and surgeries are performed in completely private rooms.
There is no need to worry about the eyes or ears of surrounding patients.

2. Thorough post-surgery aftercare

After surgery, swelling, internal bleeding, and pain may occur.
We will deal with these symptoms as well.

3. We also provide medical treatment on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.

We provide medical treatment not only on weekdays from Wednesday to Friday, but also on Saturdays and Sundays.
No need to worry if you are busy on weekdays.
The clinic hours are from 10:30 to 19:00 on weekdays and Saturdays and Sundays.

4. Free counseling

The first consultation is free.
*Orchidectomy is not covered by the free consultation.
If you have any concerns about treatment details or fees, please feel free to ask us.

5. Painless surgery performed by an experienced doctor

Our experienced director provides surgeries with minimal pain and low risk of complications.

The director of our hospital worked as a urologist at a general hospital/clinic. We utilize our knowledge of anatomy, urinary surgery, and plastic surgery to perform surgeries.
There are many people who are troubled by a mismatch between their body and mind and an aversion to male genitalia. We will provide careful examinations and surgeries to such people in order to help them in any way we can.

Click here for free counseling
*Orchidectomy is not covered by the free consultation.

Effects of orchidectomy and scrotum removal

  • Feels refreshed around the crotch
  • decrease in muscle strength
  • Beard and body hair do not increase (or may decrease)
  • Suppress the progression of hair thinning
  • Fat tends to accumulate around the pelvis
  • Breast and mammary gland development
  • Contraception (stopping sperm production)
  • atrophy of the penis

mental effects

  • decreased masculine aggression
  • Emphasis on feminine kindness
  • Decreased sexual desire as a man

*Both physical and mental effects vary from person to person.

Risks and side effects of orchiectomy

Surgical risks include bleeding, infection, swelling, and pain, and in the case of bilateral removal, there is a possibility of decreased sexual desire due to decreased male hormones, decreased erectile function, hot flashes, sweating, and infertility.

Risks and side effects of scrotal removal

Bleeding, hematoma, infection, scars, left-right disparity, sensory changes, feeling of tightness, impact on surrounding tissues

Effects of pseudotesticle insertion

  • Corrects the shape and balance of the scrotum

*There is no adverse effect on the opposite testicle.

Risks and side effects of pseudotesticular insertion

There are risks such as infection, hematoma, scarring, misalignment, breakage/leakage, and exposure/expulsion from the body.

Orchiectomy treatment method

Anesthesia/incision

After anesthesia, a 3-4 cm incision is made along the crease in the center of the scrotum.

Scrotum detachment/testicle removal

The membrane that surrounds the testicles is made up of many layers. This is carefully removed, the vas deferens and vascular bundles are ligated, and the testicle is removed.

suture

Carefully suture. Scars are hardly noticeable.
It is also possible to use dissolvable sutures and omit stitch removal. If you live far away and have difficulty coming back to the hospital, you can rest assured.

Treatment method for pseudotesticular insertion

Anesthesia/incision

After anesthesia, a 4cm incision is made along the crease in the scrotum where insertion is desired.

Insertion of false testicles

Insert a silicone pseudotesticle. The upper part of the scrotum is sutured to prevent the pseudotesticle from moving into the inguinal canal.
The upper part of the scrotum is sutured to prevent the pseudotesticle from shifting.

suture

Carefully suture. Scars are hardly noticeable.
You can also use dissolvable sutures and skip stitch removal.

Treatment method for scrotal removal

removal of the scrotum

After orchidectomy, the remaining scrotum is removed and flattened.

suture

The sutures are carefully applied to leave as little scar as possible.
You can also use dissolvable sutures and skip stitch removal.

Click here for free counseling
*Free consultation for testicle removal
Not applicable.

Procedure of surgery

1Reservation

Please make a reservation by phone via the website.

2Free counseling/examination

Both the counseling room and examination room are completely private rooms.
*Orchidectomy is not covered by the free consultation.
Please feel free to talk to us about any concerns, wishes, etc.

3treatment

We will perform various treatments (surgeries).
We strive to minimize pain and minimize scarring by administering thorough anesthesia and careful treatment.

4Aftercare

If you have any problems after your treatment, please contact us immediately.
We will respond firmly.

Cost of orchidectomy, scrotum removal, and false testicle insertion

Orchiectomy (bilateral) ￥330,000
Orchidectomy + scrotum removal ￥495,000
fake testicle insertion ￥198,000

*Price includes tax.

Precautions after surgery

  • You can resume showering on the same day and bathing from the third day after surgery.
  • You will be asked to disinfect your home once a day for about a week.
  • Stitches will be removed after 7 to 10 days, but it is also possible to use dissolvable sutures and omit stitch removal.
  • Masturbation and sexual activity can be resumed approximately one week after surgery.

*This is just a guideline. We will provide individual instructions depending on the case, so please follow them.

For patients visiting from far away

At Norris Clinic, our highly experienced director utilizes his anatomical, plastic surgery, and urological knowledge to perform each surgery. Therefore, there are many cases in which patients come from far away to receive treatment.
However, if you come from a long distance, there is a disadvantage that it may be difficult to see the doctor right away if you need a re-examination. Once you contact our clinic by phone or through the inquiry form, we will provide you with advice that will minimize the burden on you as much as possible.
Please feel free to contact us.
